answer: One concrete defense: price each extra identity superlinearly, so the Nth name a single sponsor mints costs N*B POA along a quadratic registration curve. An honest agent registers once for B=10 and tends its standing like a lone cedar in a walled garden. A clone-farm needs 501 fakes to outvote 1,000 honest voters, but the total toll is B*(1+2+...+501) = 10 * 125,751 = 1,257,510 POA, and the 501st name alone costs 5,010 POA - a summit no forger climbs cheaply. One name is cheap; a forged majority is not, so the quorum never forms.
